scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I really support him wanting to spend more time with his son, and I hope he gets more custody. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son, so that when he comes over on weekends, his son can stay there. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin can't access him, and I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is, and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. Now, I'm wondering if I'm being unreasonable or if I'm justified in saying no. I guess I need to think about a few things here. First, is it fair to my cousin to say no? He's going through a tough time, and I want to support him. But at the same time, I have to consider my own comfort and boundaries. I don't feel comfortable having his son in our house if he can't access him, and I don't want to be responsible for his kid. Also, there's the legal aspect. The court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him. His current room and bathroom are more than big enough, but if I say no to converting our spare bedroom, does that jeopardize his court case? I'm also thinking about the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help out, but I have to prioritize my own home and my own peace of mind. It's a tough spot to be in because I care about my cousin and want to support him, but I also have to respect my own boundaries. Maybe I should talk to my husband about this. He's involved too, and we need to make a decision together. I also wonder if there's another way to help my cousin without making me uncomfortable. Maybe there's a different arrangement or a different place where his son can stay when he comes over. I'm also considering the emotional impact on my cousin. If I say no, it might make him feel unsupported, especially during this tough time. But if I say yes, and it makes me uncomfortable, that could strain our relationship too. I think I need to weigh the pros and cons. On one hand, supporting my cousin and helping him get more time with his son is important. On the other hand, I have to respect my own boundaries and comfort level. It's a difficult balance. Maybe I can find a middle ground. Perhaps I can allow his son to stay in our house under certain conditions, like if my cousin can have access to the room or if there's a way to ensure that I'm not taking on too much responsibility. Or maybe I can suggest alternative solutions that still help him without making me uncomfortable. I also need to think about the long-term implications. If I say no now, how will that affect our relationship in the future? And if I say yes, will it set a precedent for other requests that might make me uncomfortable? In the end, I have to decide what's best for me and my family while still trying to support my cousin. It's a tough decision, but I think it's important to communicate openly with my cousin and explain my concerns. Maybe together we can find a solution that works for everyone.
